reviewer.actual_effort: A bounded follow-up, not a blind reading. I read all of current.json, current.xml, english-final-fixes.json and guideline-excerpts.md, and the prior reports for shards 01, 05, 06, 07 and 10. I compared the changed and in-scope English text with the full original images s125, s127, s129, s149 and s199 at display resolution (1208x2000 from 1368x2264), and opened s150 to see whether the s149 note continues there. I made no enlarged crops: every point that had changed was clear at display size. I did not open readings.json, because none of the five witnesses in scope depends on the Frankfurt service-order condition. I ran no validators, tests or renderer.

scope: English witnesses et_chil_yom_pequddah, naalah_vedin, melekh_bedin, melekh_bemishpat_yaamid_aretz and cantor_hineni only. Covered: English word-for-word text, source punctuation and encoding, the boundaries shared with the Hebrew files, and where rubrics sit. Not covered: Hebrew source accuracy.

issues.location: English naalah_vedin.xml, around segment_1 and segment_2
issues.problem: There is still a double space after 'But with', and each conditional still ends with a space just before j:endConditional. If the renderer does not collapse whitespace, the bracketed form could read '[the memory of the Shofar ]'. The Hebrew file has the same pattern. This is a markup tidy-up, not a source error.
issues.fix: Optional: move the trailing spaces outside the endConditional markers.

issues.location: English melekh_bedin.xml, around segment_1 and segment_2

issues.fix: Optional: move the spaces outside the conditionals.

issues.location: English standOff note 'Remaining verses of this poem which are of a mystical character, are', which targets …/merit
issues.problem: The note is printed after the end of the merit passage, but it targets the start of the merit prayer-part. The guidelines allow that, and the note is commentary rather than running text. The Hebrew carries a …/mystical prayer-part that the English does not. Under the Alignment rules, the Hebrew mystical section will therefore be set inside the shared merit row, beside the English merit passage. That follows from the English printing no translation, and is not a defect.
issues.fix: None required. Optional: put an anchor at the end of the merit passage and target the note there.

The rest of Hineni and the 'Vihi' paragraph match word for word and mark for mark, including 'whose name is: “I am that I am”,' and 'Love truth and peace;'. Paragraph 2 starts at the printed paragraph break, and the line-end hyphens 'im-plore' and 'ap-proach' are correctly joined. Prayer-parts /1 to /5 share their boundaries with the Hebrew, and the final terminator is present.

melekh_bemishpat_yaamid_aretz, s149: the print reads 'the sleepers of Hebron, that in their shadow'. The current comma matches. The judgment and merit passages match the image, including '(Abraham)', '(Isaac)', '(Jacob)', 'judg-ment' joined, and the closing ” after 'treasuries of clemency.'. et_chil_yom_pequddah, s125 and s127: the English runs on across the page turn, with s127 opening 'was he hewn' unindented. Both XML files now keep a single tei:p, with the page-49 pb and the part_2 milestone inside it, so the shard 01 structure note is resolved. The part_1/part_2 boundary is the same in both languages ('future | was he hewn' = 'כְּתָוֶךְ | נֶחְצַב'), and the text ends with a prayer-part terminator. Both images match word for word, including ‘Will He not do justice?’, '(Abraham)' and '(Sarah)'.

naalah_vedin, s127: the print reads 'But with the Shofar (the memory of the Shofar) I appease Him, and with bent knee, in the shelter of friends, will I sound in His garden (the Sanctuary) the shattering tone.' The unprinted English 'On Sabbath:' note has been removed. The printed parentheses are encoded as j:conditional type="marked", with no literal brackets and no instruction, which the guideline allows. The shabbat false/true conditions are kept, and the text extents match the Hebrew (בְּשׁוֹפָר and בְּזִכְרוֹן שׁוֹפָר). The Hebrew keeps its printed אם שבת inside its marked conditional. In current.json, '(the memory of the Shofar)' with marked:true is a payload view of the same thing.

melekh_bedin, s129: the print reads 'but with the Shofar (the memory of the Shofar) I appease Him, and with bent knee in the dew of revival will I sound in His garden the shattering tone.', with no comma after 'knee'. The unprinted English rubric has been removed, and the marked conditional and its extents match the Hebrew.

In all five witnesses, every English div corresp, prayer-part, chapter, verse and half-verse corresp has the same value and order as in the Hebrew file. The only exception is the Hebrew-only …/melekh_bemishpat_yaamid_aretz/mystical, which the print requires. No scope is left open.
The Hebrew incipit cues printed before the English paragraphs (את חיל, נעלה, מלך, ארץ, הנני, ויהי) are correctly left out of the English text.
